evidence: Liv. 27.11: ambiguō inter marem ac fēminam sexū īnfantem
terms.comment: Of people and animals: virīlis sexus, muliebris or fēmineus sexus; of both sexes, utrīusque sexūs. The grammatical gender of a noun is genus.

terms.gloss: sex, in the phrases virīle secus and muliebre secus
terms.comment: An old word of the historians, used as an accusative of respect: virīle secus, of the male sex (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: atque hominum genus et in sexū cōnsīderātur, virīle an muliebre sit
phrases.english: and in the case of people one considers their sex, whether male or female

phrases.latin: juvenēs utrīusque sexūs prohibuit ūllum nocturnum spectāculum frequentāre nisi cum aliquō majōre nātū propinquōrum
phrases.english: he forbade young people of both sexes to attend any show at night unless with an older relative

phrases.latin: Līberōrum capitum virīle secus ad decem mīlia capta
phrases.english: about ten thousand free persons of the male sex were taken
